notes: An after-action report. About 40 seconds after you finish a mission, the tracker asks a few quick questions about what it actually involved — how hard it was, whether you needed a crew. Your answers go to subliminal.gg and build a picture of each mission that the game files alone cannot give: the game knows what a mission awards, not what it is like to run.

A setup wizard on first run. If you install the app without going through the website first, it now walks you through finding your game log, connecting your account, and reviewing your settings. It skips anything already done, so nothing is asked twice. Reachable any time from the tray, under Run setup again.

Settings is now a panel on the overlay. It opens where the rest of the app lives, and you can place, resize and skin it like any other widget instead of it being a separate window over the game. Open it from the cog or the tray, the same as before.

The overlay now appears in Alt-Tab. Switch to it and you get your real mouse cursor back across the whole overlay, which makes reaching the cog and the smaller widgets much easier than guessing where the pointer went. Switch back and clicks go straight to the game again.

The scan read area shows itself. Open the Mining Scanner and the outline is simply there, rather than waiting to be found in a settings menu. A Hide button on the box itself turns it off if you would rather not see it.

The Mining Scanner stops reading the screen when it is closed. Previously the opt-in alone kept it scanning every few seconds whether or not the widget was open. Auto-show still works — that is the one case where it is closed on purpose and needs the read to open itself.
Fixed: the SC Feed card that appeared at launch and never went away. It now behaves like any other notification and clears itself. While it was up it could also swallow clicks meant for the game.
Fixed: turning a widget on while in arrange mode left it out of arrange, with no drag handles, until you left and re-entered.
Fixed: the app icon now shows on its windows instead of the default Electron one.

Also: opt-in prompts to tick blueprints the fabricator shows you already own but the app has no record of (off by default), and the diagnostics report now says where settings are saved and whether saving actually worked.

Fixes the terminal window that 0.1.35 left sitting on your desktop. The overlay runs a small background service, and on Windows a service like that gets given a console window unless the app explicitly says not to — 0.1.35 stopped hiding it. Nothing was wrong with the service itself; it just became visible. It is hidden again.

New widget — Unlock Alerts. The "Blueprint Received" pop used to be stuck to the bottom of the tracker panel, which is the one place you never look mid-mission. It is now its own widget you drag wherever you actually watch, it shows the item's picture, and several unlocks at once queue up instead of stepping on each other.

The Web Page widget can show ANY site now. Sites that refuse to be embedded — the RSI site above all, plus UEX, erkul and starcitizen.tools — used to come up as a blank box. They work. Sign-ins work too, in their own cookie jar, kept separate from your normal browser.

You can send Twitch chat from the overlay. Sign in with Twitch in the chat widget (a short code on twitch.tv, no password typed into the app) and the send bar appears. Reading chat still needs no account at all.

Blueprint unlocks show the real fabricator photo instead of a grey 3D model. The old picture was shared between items that use the same game model, so three different Scraper Modules all looked identical — it could not even tell you which one you had unlocked.

Far fewer phantom "Debris" call-outs while mining. Three things were making noise: the app announced anything it read even when you were not scanning, ordinary HUD lettering could be misread as a number, and a scan from ages ago was re-announced every time the widget reloaded. It now checks the frame for the marker beside a real signature, ignores stale scans, and there is a "Call out debris & unknown" switch in the Mining Scanner settings if you only care about ore.

The scanner stops guessing. Debris comes in whole salvage panels, so a debris signature is always a multiple of 2,000 — that, rather than "it wasn't in my rock list", is now what makes it debris. A signature that is neither ore nor a panel count gets an honest "I don't know what that is, but it's not ore" (five ways, at random) instead of a wrong "Debris", and a number too big for the game to have shown is thrown out as a misread.

And when a signature could be either — 16,000 is five Savrilium rocks AND eight debris panels — it says so instead of picking one. You get "Debris, or Savrilium", or "This could be Savrilium" if it's a rock you've targeted, and it always speaks up: either way you have to fly over and look.

New in the Mining Scanner's settings — "Show the scan read area". It draws a box over the part of the screen the app reads for a signature, and you can DRAG it (or its corner) to move and resize that area, with a Reset if you want the default back. Useful if your HUD sits somewhere unusual, or Star Citizen is on a different monitor than the app expects.

That box now also prints the number it just read, centred underneath it, so you can hold it up against the real signature on your screen. A number with a line through it is one the app read but did not act on. It also disappears when you close the Mining Scanner, instead of being left on your screen.

Sixes and eights that come out as each other are now corrected. A signature is only ever one of about 165 possible numbers, so a misread usually lands on a value that cannot exist — and there is normally exactly one real number a single wrong digit away. When there is, the app uses it, so a rock the scanner used to shrug at gets named. When two rocks are both possible it says nothing rather than guess at one, and it never "corrects" a number that was already valid.

You can REMOVE a hotkey now, not just change it. Each row in Settings → Hotkeys has an ✕; clearing one leaves that action with no key at all and it stays cleared. (Clearing the hold-to-interact key also turns that mode off, since without the key nothing on the overlay would be clickable.)

The patch notes window no longer runs off the screen. On a multi-monitor setup it sized itself against every monitor put together, so with a tall second display it could grow past the top and bottom of the screen it was centred on and take the ✕ and "Got it" with it. It is capped now, and the notes scroll inside it.
Widget names are clearer: Mission & BP Tracker, Mining Scanner, Journal, Loot Split, Event Tracker and Infographic Viewer. Your layout, hotkeys and settings are untouched — only the labels changed.

The settings cog no longer sits there forever. If you summon it and go back to flying, it packs itself away after 30 seconds of the game having focus — it was holding the overlay in a clickable state the whole time it stayed open.

New in Settings — a "Copy diagnostics" button. If something is not working, it copies a short report (is the background service answering, is your game.log being found and read, which dataset is loaded, which opt-ins are on, are you running as admin) that you can paste into a bug report. No passwords or tokens in it.

The tracker panel now tells you what your next rank actually unlocks. Battaglia hands out ships at certain ranks — the Golem, Prospector and MOLE — and the standing bar used to be a bare number with no reason to care about it.
Missions that list two reputation awards against the same standing no longer show as two confusing identical rows. You get the one that counts, with the extra disclosed rather than silently dropped.

Fixes: the SC Feed widget's alert settings (the ♪ button) open again; the tilt slider works on every widget that has one; the Mining Scanner wears your ship's skin properly and lost its slab of empty glass; the Web Page widget's bar now slides out on hover like every other widget; and dragging a widget no longer gets yanked off course by Star Citizen recentring your mouse.
Behind the scenes: if the overlay's background service ever crashes it now writes down why and restarts itself, instead of leaving the app looking fine while nothing works.

The overlay is now a widget canvas — nine widgets you place, size and stack anywhere on screen: the Blueprint tracker, Mining Assistant, Notepad, Twitch Chat, SC Feed news, Party Split, a Battaglia grind tracker, any Web Page, and your Binding Chart. Drag one widget onto another's bar to GROUP them into a tabbed stack, and pop a tab back out whenever you like.
Every widget has the same hover bar now: move, reset, its own settings, and close — plus a text-size control (70–200%) so anything stays readable from 1080p to 4K.

Dragging is fixed. A widget used to freeze when you dragged it near another one and then jump to catch up — the neighbouring widget was swallowing the mouse. It tracks your cursor properly now, and every widget's bar comes out while you drag so you can see where a stack will land.
Reset puts a widget back in the MIDDLE of your screen, and the settings cog has a reset button for each widget — so a widget dragged off the edge of your monitor is always recoverable.
Hold-to-interact only applies while Star Citizen is in front. If you're on the desktop the overlay just works like a normal window, so your interact key no longer types into Discord or your browser.

A closed widget now really is closed — it stops polling, drops its connections and frees its memory instead of quietly running in the background. The Mining Assistant also stays properly silent when it's off screen or tabbed behind another widget.

Fixes: grouping the Battaglia tracker with the mission tracker no longer hides the tab bar; the Twitch Chat and Notepad bars retract again once you move away; and the Blueprint panel's settings menu opens beside its cog instead of off the top of the panel.
Lighter on your machine: the screen-reading loop no longer launches a Windows helper process every three seconds, and the overlay does less work while your cursor is nowhere near it.

New Notepad widget — jot notes right on the overlay. Make as many titled notes as you like; they autosave, and you can drag the box bigger and bump the text size to suit any monitor. Turn it on from the settings cog's widget list or the tray. To type while you're in the game, click "Type" — it grabs the keyboard and frees up your interact key so you're not alt-tabbing.

New "Blueprint Received" pop — the moment you collect any blueprint it flashes the item and name, no matter which mission you're tracking. Handy when you've got several of the same mission on the go and the receipt used to land on one you weren't looking at.

The idle screen (when nothing's tracked) now shows your reputation and aUEC per hour — both what you earned in the last hour and your current grind pace. aUEC shows "—" for missions the game doesn't report a payout for (most of them right now).

"Guaranteed rewards" are now "Physical Rewards" — the actual items/ships a mission hands over (the game never tells the app when you get these). Tick one off once it's in your hangar and it tucks away under a "Received" list, so you can keep track of what you've collected.
New "Patch notes" button in the settings cog — pop this What's New card back up any time.
Fixed the What's New card opening half on one monitor and half on the other — it now centers on your main display.
Fixed Quantum Drive names (like the XL-1) not being recognized at the Fabrication Kiosk, so their images can be captured and contributed now.
Fixed dark, low-contrast items (black visors, dark-finish armor) getting clipped in captured item images.
Much sharper item reading at the Fabrication Kiosk — a new, more accurate text reader handles the stylized kiosk fonts (item names, "Tier", ship-component names) that the old one sometimes mangled.
The overlay now reads only the monitor your game is on, and only the part of the screen it needs — so multi-monitor setups no longer accidentally read the wrong display.

What's New tidy-up: each version now shows its release date and time (UTC), older versions are collapsed by default so the card stays short, the close button can never end up off-screen, and it no longer hides itself after one look unless you tick "Don't show this again".
The fabricator reader can no longer get stuck — if a scan or upload ever hangs, it recovers on its own instead of sitting on "Reading the fabricator…" until you restart the app.

Captured item images upload reliably now: a failed upload retries by itself, and on startup the app re-checks and sends up any captures that never made it to the site — no more "it said it saved but never showed up."

Clearer scanning status — the overlay names the item it's reading, and tells you the truth about uploads: "shared" only once the picture is actually on the site, "upload failed — retrying" otherwise (no more misleading "saved").
The What's New card now shows the last several versions, so if you've been away for a bit you can catch up on everything you missed — not just the newest patch.
New Consolidated Outland skin — hop in a Nomad and the overlay picks up its frosty ice-cyan HUD. Grey's now shows its logo in the folder-tab too.
Updated for the latest patch with fuller crafting recipes, mining and commodity data, and a much larger set of mission payouts.
The mission-complete card shows the mission's payout again — read from the game data now that the game stopped logging the award.

Streamers: the overlay broadcasts the manufacturer of the ship you're flying, so your other stream overlays can re-color to match it live. Plus a new "switch back to Mobiglas when I leave my ship" option.
Fixed the binding-chart PNG picker in Settings rendering as a tiny box with no room for the filename.

Fixed ship components (quantum drives, shields and the like) not scanning at the Fabrication Kiosk on 4K/high-scale displays — the reader now tolerates OCR glitches in the kiosk text, and when it truly can't read an item it tells you instead of sitting silently on "Watching Star Citizen…".
Manufacturer skins now stay pinned for active Twitch subscribers — connect the tracker to subliminal.gg and link your Twitch, and your chosen skin sticks instead of reverting after the preview.
Multi-monitor: in Arrange mode you can now drag a widget onto a second display — it crosses seamlessly and stays there, and the Arrange controls always stay on your primary monitor.

Manufacturer skins! The overlay now automatically matches the ship you're flying — Drake, Aegis, Crusader, RSI, MISC, Origin and more. Free on 'Auto'; subscribers can pin one manufacturer to use it regardless of ship.
Each skin shows its manufacturer logo in a folder-tab on the panel, with brand-specific corner details, dividers, and a reputation bar tinted to match the theme.

Smarter blueprint image capture: items that render as a dark schematic (like quantum drives) are now captured instead of skipped, and same-name size variants (e.g. the mining lasers) resolve to the right one.
Fixed same-named blueprints (like the three Cinch Scraper Modules) so they all share the item image instead of only one showing a picture.
New name: this is now SC Overlay. It's grown well past just blueprints — mining, loadouts, and more — so the name caught up. Your settings and your whole collection carry over untouched.

The Mining Assistant is now part of the main overlay instead of its own separate window. That fixes the annoying stuff: clicking one widget while another's open just works now, and nothing steals a click you meant for the game.

A much cleaner Settings page. Everything's sorted into categories with the opt-in features up top, each setting is a single line with an ⓘ you can hover for the details, and changes save the moment you make them — no more hunting for a Save button.

New: put a widget on a second monitor or your phone. Settings now gives you copy-ready links for the Blueprint and Mining widgets (and OBS browser-source URLs), including one that works from your phone on the same Wi-Fi.
The mining scanner now ignores tiny signatures under 2,000, so it stops calling out every little scrap of debris.
New: partner promos in Settings — deals from the brands that support the channel, at no extra cost to you.

New: the overlay is now an “overlay app” — the Blueprint tracker and Mining Assistant float freely on your screen. Drag them anywhere, resize each from its corner, and give each its own angle so a left and a right widget can lean in toward you.

New: an Arrange mode that moves everything at once. Grab a widget's ⠿ handle (or press Ctrl+Alt+M) and the whole screen shows it's in edit mode — drag, resize, then hit Done. Your layout is saved and survives updates.

New: a settings menu that appears top-right whenever you're working with the overlay — widget on/off, theme, and a way into everything. It fades away when you're done so it's not in your face while you fly.
The Mining Assistant now matches your ship's theme too — hop in a Drake and it goes gunmetal-and-orange right alongside the tracker.
Widgets now sit flat by default with a slight inward tilt; set each one's exact angle in its ⚙. And these patch notes now pop up in the middle of the screen on launch.
Fixed: “Restart as administrator” now actually relaunches the app elevated. It was closing the tracker and never reopening it, leaving stray processes you had to kill by hand — that's sorted.

New: the Mining Assistant — a second overlay window (tray → Mining Assistant, or press Shift+F3) that names rocks from the mining scanner's signature, counts down your refinery jobs and alarms when they finish, and calls out your target rocks in the HAL voice. It matches the main overlay's look and stays click-through until you hover it, so you won't nudge it mid-flight.

Fixed: your hotkeys now work while Star Citizen is focused, not just when you alt-tab to the desktop. If they still don't fire in-game, open Settings → In-Game Hotkeys and hit “Restart as administrator”.
Fixed: opening an overlay (like the binding chart) can no longer bury the Settings window — Settings now always stays on top.
Fixed: two features can no longer grab the same hotkey by accident.

New: a reputation bar in Mission Info shows your current standing with each mission giver (e.g. Sr. Contractor) and how close you are to the next rank — worked out from the missions you've completed since the last wipe. Hit “Verify from logs” in the ⚙ to fill it in from your play history.
Fixed: your tracked missions no longer disappear when you relaunch or Alt-F4 back into the game — they were getting wiped on every login.
Fixed: blueprint pools no longer show duplicate entries. On newer game builds the tracker could fall back to an older, stale copy of the mission data.
The opt-in mission-name scanner now reads mining, scanning and most other mission types, not only “Go to” missions.

Fixed: missions that don't place a map marker — mining, ore scanning and friends — used to show nothing at all. They now resolve their blueprint pool and appear in the mission picker like everything else.
New: your rank with each mission giver, worked out from the highest-rank mission you've been offered. Hit “Verify from logs” in the ⚙ to backfill it from your play history.
The guaranteed rewards and the random blueprint pool are now clearly separated — the pool says “1 random blueprint per completion”, because that's what it is.
Guaranteed item rewards now have their own tick box, so you can check off the ones you've picked up (kept separate from your blueprint count).
The owned count moved up next to the mission name — the ⚙ and move handle were sitting on top of it.
A long blueprint pool no longer pushes the panel sideways into a horizontal scrollbar.
The header now reads “Active Mission” instead of a second “Blueprint Pool”.
New: the overlay diamond glows purple when SubliminalsTV is live on Twitch — hover it and click to jump into the stream.
In the Fabricator, the diamond glows gold so you can tell the tracker sees the kiosk.
Both opt-in screen-reading features (pinned-mission scan + item-image capture) now appear in Settings and the overlay ⚙, and stay in sync.
Open the full Settings window straight from the overlay ⚙.
Pasting a sync token now turns syncing on automatically — no more forgetting the checkbox.
New: a settings ⚙ on the overlay — the odds view (base / your real odds) and “Verify from logs” now live in there, and you can hide the category filter bar, for a cleaner HUD.
Cleaner footer: your Collected count is now big and clear, with the tracker version and game build stacked neatly beside it.
The overlay now shows what the item-image scanner is doing — a quick toast when it reads your pinned mission or captures a fabricator item, plus a live status in the ⚙ menu.
New: toggle mission-name scanning on/off from the overlay ⚙ menu (reads the mission you have pinned in-game — off by default).
Fixed: the pinned-mission reader now recognizes missions whose names are cut off on-screen or contain quotes (e.g. Terrorist Shigemori "Jester" Amsden…).
Mission Info (faction / type / reputation) now opens by default.
Settings tidied up for the blueprint tracker.
Mission-Complete card now shows the actual item render for each blueprint you unlock — one big image for a single drop, a grid for more.
New: opt-in log sharing (Settings) — help improve mission & blueprint detection. Your handle, account, IP and chat are stripped before anything is sent. Off by default.
Recent lists can now show relative time ("2h ago") or the exact date & clock — toggle in Settings.
Settings window restyled to match subliminal.gg.
The tracker's source code is now public on GitHub.
